title: Health check after 60
what: A routine health check for people over 60. The doctor checks blood pressure, blood sugar, heart, memory, vision, and fall risk.
why: Once a year or on schedule, to catch conditions early and adjust medicines.
duration: usually 1 to 2 visits; test results in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: All the medicines you take, including herbs and supplements
If your memory, sleep, hearing, or vision has gotten worse

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Put all your medicine packs in a bag and bring them.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood is usually taken in the morning on an empty stomach. Plain water is fine. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Morning medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor whether to take morning medicines before the tests.

bring: All your medicines, or a list
Past test results and discharge papers
Glasses and a hearing aid, if you use them
steps: You give blood and urine samples
The nurse checks your blood pressure, weight, and height
An ECG and other listed tests are done
The doctor asks how you feel and about your medicines
A few questions about memory and mood
The results and plan are discussed with you
feel: Usually nothing unpleasant, except the needle for the blood test
You may get tired. Bring water and a snack
after: The doctor may adjust your medicines. Do not change them on your own
If needed, you will be referred to specialists
Discuss vaccines for older adults with your doctor

faq.a: The doctor will check for duplicates and how they work together. This matters more with age.

faq.q: Can I bring a family member?
faq.a: Yes, it often helps. They can remember the doctor's advice.

reminders.text: Health check tomorrow. Bring all your medicines and your ID. Tests in the morning on an empty stomach. Water is fine.
